Progress of long computations

Source: R/progress.R
riskmap_progress.Rd

RiskMap shows how far a long computation has gone and about how long it has left.

  • parametric_bootstrap(), profile.RiskMap(), assess_prediction() and assess_simulation() show a progress bar with the work done and an estimate of the time left.

  • predict.RiskMap() shows a bar while it predicts at many locations in blocks, and while it propagates parameter uncertainty over its parameter draws.

  • glgpm() shows a line for each stage of Monte Carlo maximum likelihood, with the time the stage took. While a stage runs, the line has a spinner and the time so far, which move each time the likelihood is evaluated. A step computed in one call to compiled code, such as the Langevin sampler, shows its line without them.

Progress is shown when the function's argument messages is TRUE and the option RiskMap.progress is TRUE. The option's default is rlang::is_interactive(), so progress appears in the console but not in scripts run with Rscript, in documents rendered by knitr or in tests, even when these are started from the console. Set options(RiskMap.progress = TRUE) to show it in the log of a script too. A log can't redraw a line, so there a bar writes a line each time another tenth of the work is done, and each stage of a fit writes a line when it starts and another, with its time, when it ends. options(RiskMap.progress = FALSE) hides progress everywhere and leaves the other messages.

The bars are drawn by the cli package, so its options apply as well. For example, a bar appears only once a computation has run for getOption("cli.progress_show_after", 2) seconds.

Examples

# Show progress in the log of a script
options(RiskMap.progress = TRUE)

# Hide it everywhere
options(RiskMap.progress = FALSE)
